title: Reward Modeling
oneLine: Learn a scalar reward from human preference comparisons.

paras: You cannot write down a loss for 'a helpful answer', but people can compare two answers and say which is better. A reward model learns a scalar score from many such comparisons, so that preferred responses score higher. That learned reward is what RLHF then optimizes the policy against.
The Bradley-Terry model turns score differences into preference probabilities:
sections.texNote: Train r by maximizing the log-likelihood of the observed preferences.

sections.code:
# pairwise preference loss (chosen > rejected)
loss = -np.log(sigmoid(r(chosen) - r(rejected))).mean()
sections.caption: Push the chosen response's score above the rejected one's.

takeaways: Reward models learn from pairwise preferences, not absolute labels.
Bradley-Terry links score gaps to preference probabilities.
Goodhart risk: optimizing a proxy reward invites reward hacking.
